podcast.body: This song became a hit for Fats Domino after its co-writer, Lewis, was brought out of retirement by Don Kirshner. Lewis had co-written the song decades earlier, having been a hit songwriter in the 1930s and 1940s. "But then Fat Stomano have had a hit with Blueberry Hill, a song Lewis had co-written decades earlier."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.body: This song, originally written in 1940 by Vincent Rose, Larry Stock, and Al Lewis, became Fats Domino's biggest hit, climbing to number two on the pop charts. Despite producer Dave Bartholomew's initial reluctance and attempt to prevent its release, engineer Bunny Robin expertly pieced together a complete version from disparate half-finished takes, aided by drummer Earl Palmer's precise timing. "The song became Domino's biggest hit, rising to number two in the pop charts."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
